## INVESTIGATION RESULT — the premise is a false positive; verdict HISTORICAL-ONLY / NO DEFECT

### 1. None of the six carries a FORCE_CLOSE audit record (VERIFIED)

A real FORCE_CLOSE audit record is a COMMENT whose body starts `FORCE_CLOSE:`
(`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:435-441`). Re-checked all six via `show_ticket`:

| ticket | FORCE_CLOSE comment? | what the scan actually matched |
|---|---|---|
| 119f-63e3-34b7-4f96 | none | COMPLETION_VERDICT prose quoting *other* tickets' FORCE_CLOSE comments |
| 145e-52a9-26e3-4209 | none | REVIEW_RESULT quoting a checklist item that contains the words `FORCE_CLOSE` |
| 93d0-adbb-f982-4d39 | none | COMPLETION_VERDICT naming the eval category `FORCE_CLOSED` |
| 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d | none | REVIEW_RESULT evidence quoting 2c14/8a4b's FORCE_CLOSE comments |
| e879-2d83-e925-4f2b | none | REVIEW_RESULT quoting parent 01e8's FORCE_CLOSE comment |
| e95e-1543-cac7-47b9 | none | its own description text: "there is NO REOPEN/FORCE_CLOSE event type" |

Every reported "last force" timestamp maps to an LLM-authored REVIEW_RESULT / COMPLETION_VERDICT
or a description, never to an audit record. The prior scan substring-matched serialized event JSON
and caught prose. That also explains e95e's "signature before force-close": the "force" is a
SNAPSHOT of its own description. **The op-cert-service hypothesis is unnecessary — nothing needs
explaining.** ("146 force-closed tickets" is also inflated; the precise count is 128.)

Note for future scans: compiled comments use key `body`, not `text` — a scan on `text` returns 0.

### 2. force-close has NEVER been able to sign (VERIFIED)

`close_precheck.py:176-177` — `if force_close: return None  # close, but withhold the signed
confirmation` — returns before any verify/disposition branch, and `transition_close.py:365` signs
only `if target_status == "closed" and verified_result is not None`. `git log -S` puts that guard in
`85a77b9cc8` (2026-06-18), the commit that introduced the close gate itself. So a force-close today
**cannot** mint a completion attestation, and never could. Empirically confirmed by 43ea-3d5a-078f-4fe3
force-closed today: two `certifiable: true` COMPLETION_VERDICT events, zero completion-verifier
attestation. **738a is NOT the fix** — it added disposition-close attestation (`close_disposition.py`)
and mutation-checked the pre-existing guard; it did not create it.

### 3. The real population is 13 tickets, disjoint from the six (VERIFIED)

Precise scan (real `FORCE_CLOSE:` comment AND a completion-verifier attestation): 13 tickets.
Seven show the documented reopen -> in_progress -> re-close remedy with `last_reopened_at` between
force and signature (ce94, b043, fc2a, 1787, 297d, 8d27, 2bc7) — correct and benign. The other six
(cbc6, c7c5, ce75, be08, 57d6, 72d5) are all dated **2026-06-18 to 2026-06-26** and lack
`last_reopened_at` — but that field was only introduced 2026-06-30 (`66f0220d74`, epic
dark-acme-lumen). Their absent reopen marker is the field not existing yet, not an absent reopen
(72d5 even carries a post-force "Completion Verification — PASS" comment). INFERRED, not verified:
their pre-close history was compacted away, so the reopen STATUS events are unrecoverable.

### 4. Integrity impact: none (VERIFIED)

`child_closure_findings` (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py:89-103`) treats a force-closed **or reopened**
child as uncertified and withholds the parent's signature; it checks signature *validity*, not mere
presence. Since no force-close can mint an attestation, and post-reopen signatures are the intended
remedy, nothing false-certifies.

### Recommendation

Close this as **not-a-defect / invalid premise**. The four acceptance criteria are moot: there is no
population to trace. If the operator wants residual value, the one real follow-up is a hardening
ticket for the scan methodology (match structured records, not serialized-JSON substrings) — the
description's own "Method note" already anticipated exactly this failure mode.
